τινός ἐστιν ἢ τινῶν πρῶτον. τίνες οὖν δεύτερον ἐπιστεύθησαν ἰδεῖν ἐστὶν ἐκ τοῦ ᾧ
μὲν γὰρ διὰ τοῦ πνεύματο δίδοται λόγο οφία καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. εἰ δέ τις συγχεόμενος
ταὐτὸν οἴεται τὰ λόγια τοῦ θεοῦ τοῖς γράμμασι τοῦ θεοῦ, προσεχέτω τῷ λέγοντι
ψαλμῷ τὰ λόγια κυρίου λόγια ἁγνὰ ἀργύριον πεπυρωμένον δοκίμιον τῇ γῇ
κεκαθαρι μένον ἑπταπλα ίω . ἐγὼ μὲν γὰρ οὐκ οἶμαι τὰ ἁγνὰ λόγια εἶναι τὰ αὐτὰ τῷ
ἀποκτείννυντι γράμματι. ὥσπερ δὲ οἱ προειρημένοι Ἰουδαῖοι πρῶτοι ἐπιστεύθησαν
τὰ λόγια τοῦ θεοῦ, οὕτως καί τινες ἠπίστησαν· ἀλλ' οὐχὶ τῶν τοιούτων εἴτε πρὸς τὸν
θεὸν εἴτε πρὸς τὰ λόγια αὐτοῦ ἀπιστία τὴν πίστιν τοῦ θεοῦ καταργήσει. ποίαν δὲ
πίστιν τοῦ θεοῦ; πότερον ἣν θεὸς πιστεύει τισὶ τὰ λόγια; ἢ ἣν οἱ πιστευθέντες τὰ
λόγια πιστεύουσι τῷ θεῷ, ὡς Ἀβραὰμ ἐπί τευ ε τῷ θεῷ καὶ ἐλογί θη αὐτῷ εἰ
δικαιο ύνην; ἑκάτερον οἶμαι λόγον ἔχειν· μεμνῆσθαι γὰρ δεῖ τόν τε πιστεύοντα τῷ
θεῷ καὶ τὸν πεπιστευμένον τὰ λόγια αὐτοῦ, μάλιστα ἐν καιρῷ τῆς τῶν ἀπίστων
χλεύης ἣν χλευάζουσι τοὺς πεπιστευκότας, τοῦ μὴ καταργεῖσθαι τὴν πίστιν τοῦ θεοῦ
ὑπὸ τοῦ λόγου τῶν ἀπιστούντων. 12 iii 4 γινέσθω δὲ ὁ θεὸς ἀληθὴς πᾶς δὲ ἄνθρωπος
ψεύστης· καθὼς γέγραπται· ὅπως ἂν δικαιωθῇς ἐν τοῖς λόγοις σου καὶ νικήσῃς ἐν τῷ
κρίνεσθαί σε. τὸ οὖν γενηθήτω εἴρηται ἀντὶ εὐκτικοῦ, ὡς τὸ εἴη τὸ ὄνομά ου
εὐλογημένον εἰ τοὺ αἰῶνα . 13 ιιι 9–18 τί οὖν; προεχόμεθα; οὐ πάντως·
προῃτιασάμεθα γὰρ Ἰουδαίους τε καὶ Ἕλληνας πάντας ὑφ' ἁμαρτίαν εἶναι καθὼς
γέγραπται· οὐκ ἐστὶν δίκαιος οὐδὲ εἷς· οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ συνιών· οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ ἐκζητῶν τὸν
θεόν· πάντες ἐξέκλιναν, ἅμα ἠχρειώθησαν· οὐκ ἔστιν ποιῶν χρηστότητα, οὐκ ἔστιν
ἕως ἑνός· τάφος ἀνεῳγμένος ὁ λάρυγξ αὐτῶν· ταῖς γλώσσαις αὐτῶν ἐδολιοῦσαν· ἰὸς
ἀσπίδων ὑπὸ τὰ χείλη αὐτῶν· ὧν τὸ στόμα ἀρᾶς καὶ πικρίας γέμει· ὀξεῖς οἱ πόδες
αὐτῶν ἐκχέαι αἷμα· σύντριμμα καὶ ταλαιπωρία ἐν ταῖς ὁδοῖς αὐτῶν καὶ ὁδὸν εἰρήνης
οὐκ ἔγνωσαν· οὐκ ἔστιν φόβος θεοῦ ἀπέναντι τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν. βούλεται ῥητὰ
συναγαγεῖν πῶς ἅπαντες Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ Ἕλληνες ὑπὸ ἁμαρτίαν γεγόνασιν, ἀρξάμενος
ἀπὸ τοῦ καθὼς γέγραπται οὐκ ἔστιν δίκαιος οὐδὲ εἷς, οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ συνιών, οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ
ἐκζητῶν τὸν θεόν· ὅπερ αὐταῖς λέξεσιν οὐχ εὕρομέν που γεγραμμένον, ἀλλὰ
νομίζομεν ἀπὸ τοῦ τρισκαιδεκάτου ψαλμοῦ καὶ τοῦ νβʹ μεταπεποιῆσθαι ὑπὸ τοῦ
ἀποστόλου τὰ ῥητά· ἐν μὲν γὰρ τῷ ιγʹ ψαλμῷ εἴρηται κύριο ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ
διέκυψεν ἐπὶ τοὺ υἱοὺ τῶν ἀνθρώπων τοῦ ἰδεῖν εἰ ἔ τιν υνιὼν ἢ ἐκζητῶν τὸν θεόν·
ἐν δὲ τῷ νβʹ ὁ θεὸ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ διέκυψεν ἐπὶ τοὺ υἱοὺ τῶν ἀνθρώπων τοῦ ἰδεῖν
εἰ ἔ τι υνιὼν ἢ ἐκζητῶν τὸν θεόν. ἔοικεν οὖν νενοηκέναι ἰσοδυναμεῖν τὸ τοῦ ἰδεῖν εἰ
ἔ τι υνιὼν ἢ ἐκζητῶν τὸν θεὸν τῷ οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ συνιών, οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ ἐκζητῶν τὸν
θεόν. καὶ τὸ οὐκ ἔστι δίκαιος οὐδὲ εἷς νομίζω γεγονέναι ἐκ τοῦ οὐκ ἔ τι ποιῶν
χρη τότητα, οὐκ ἔ τιν ἕω ἑνό · ὥστε τῇ δυνάμει δὶς αὐτὸν τεθεικέναι, ἅπαξ μὲν
μεταποιήσαντα, ἅπαξ δὲ λέξεσι ταῖς αὐταῖς χρησάμενον, καὶ παραλιπόντα τὸ
δεύτερον εἰρημένον οὐκ ἔστιν. τὸ δὲ ἰὸς ἀσπίδων ὑπὸ τὰ χείλη αὐτῶν, αὐταῖς λέξεσι
κεῖται ἡ χρῆσις ἐν τῷ ρλθʹ ψαλμῷ· τὸ δ' ἐπὶ τούτοις ὧν τὸ στόμα ἀρᾶς καὶ πικρίας
γέμει ἔοικεν γεγονέναι ἀπὸ τοῦ ἐν τῷ ἐνάτῳ ψαλμῷ οὕτως εἰρημένου οὗ ἀρᾶ τὸ
τόμα αὐτοῦ γέμει καὶ πικρία καὶ δόλου. εἶθ' ἑξῆς τοῦτο ἐστιν· ὀξεῖς οἱ πόδες αὐτῶν
ἐκχέαι αἷμα· τοῦτο δὲ ζητήσεις ἐν τῷ Ἠσαίᾳ, ἢ ἐν ταῖς ἄλλαις τῶν Παροιμιῶν
ἐκδόσεσιν, ἐν τῷ ταχεινοὶ ἐκχέαι αἷμα, ὃ μετὰ ἀστερίσκων προσετέθη ἐν τῇ ἐκδόσει
τῶν ἑβδομήκοντα. τὸ δὲ σύντριμμα καὶ ταλαιπωρία ἐν ταῖς ὁδοῖς αὐτῶν μέχρι τοῦ
δεῦρο οὐκ οἶδα ποῦ ἀνεγνωκώς· οἶμαι δὲ ἐν τινὶ τῶν προφητῶν γεγράφθαι τὸ ὁδὸν
εἰρήνης οὐκ ἔγνωσαν, ἐν δὲ ψαλμοῖς οὐκ ἔστιν φόβος θεοῦ ἀπέναντι τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν
αὐτῶν. πλήθους δὲ ὄντων ἁμαρτημάτων, οὐ πάντως ἕκαστος ἔνοχός ἐστι τοῖς
ἅπασιν, ἀλλ' οἱ μὲν τῷδε τῷ ἁμαρτήματι οἱ δὲ τῷδε, καὶ οὕτω τοὺς πάντας τοῖς
πᾶσιν. 14 ιιι 19, 20 οἴδαμεν γὰρ ὅτι ὅσα ὁ νόμος λέγει τοῖς ἐν τῷ νόμῳ λαλεῖ, ἵνα πᾶν
στόμα φραγῇ καὶ ὑπόδικος γένηται πᾶς ὁ κόσμος τῷ θεῷ· διότι ἐξ ἔργων νόμου οὐ
δικαιωθήσεται πᾶσα σὰρξ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ· διὰ γὰρ νόμου ἐπίγνωσις ἁμαρτίας. τί
κοινὸν πρὸς πᾶσαν σάρκα τὰ ἔργα τοῦ Μωσέως νόμου; πῶς δὲ καὶ τῆς ἁμαρτίας
ἐπίγνωσις διὰ τοῦ νόμου Μωυσέως γίνεται, πολλῶν καὶ πρὸ Μωσέως ἐπεγνωκότων
τὰ ἴδια ἁμαρτήματα; Κάιν μὲν γάρ φησι μείζων ἡ αἰτία μου τοῦ ἀφεθῆναί με· οἱ δὲ εἰς
Αἴγυπτον καταβάντες πρὸς τὸν Ἰωσὴφ πατριάρχαι λέγουσιν ἐπὶ τοῖς τοῦ Ἰωσὴφ πρὸς
pass_a_gloss: Who is it or what things first? Then which were entrusted second to see, it is from the one for through the spirit is given word serpent and the following. But if someone confused thinks the oracles of God are the writings of God, let them attend to the speaker psalm the oracles of the Lord pure words silver refined in fire tested on the earth purified sevenfold. For I indeed do not think the pure words are the same as the killing letter. Just as the previously mentioned Jews were entrusted first with the oracles of God, so also some disbelieved; but not that such unbelief whether toward God or toward his oracles nullifies the faith of God. What then is the faith of God? Is it which God believes in some the oracles? Or is it which those entrusted with the oracles believe in God, as Abraham believed in God and it was counted to him as righteousness? Both I think have reason; for one must remember both the one believing in God and the one entrusted with his oracles, especially in the time of the scoffing of the unbelievers by whom they scoff those who have believed, so that the faith of God may not be nullified by the word of the unbelievers. Let God be true though every human a liar, as it is written, so that you may be justified in your words and prevail when you are judged. Therefore let it be said instead of optative, as may the name of you blessed be to the ages. What then? Shall we excel? Not at all; for we have accused both Jews and Greeks all under sin, as it is written: there is none righteous, not even one; there is none who understands; there is none who seeks God; all have turned aside, together become useless; there is none doing kindness, not even one; their throat is an open grave; with their tongues they practice deceit; the venom of asps is under their lips; whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness; their feet are swift to shed blood; destruction and misery are in their ways, and the way of peace they have not known; there is no fear of God before their eyes. He desires to gather explicitly how both Jews and Greeks have become under sin, starting from what is written: there is none righteous, not even one; there is none who understands; there is none who seeks God. Which we have not found written in those words, but we think taken from the thirteenth psalm and the twenty-fifth, having been changed by the apostle: in the eighteenth psalm it says the Lord from heaven looked down on the sons of men to see if there was one who understands or seeks God; and in the twenty-fifth, God from heaven looked down on the sons of men to see if there was one who understands or seeks God. It seems then they have considered equal the act of seeing whether there is one who understands or seeks God with there is none who understands, there is none who seeks God. And I think the notion of none righteous not even one has come from not doing kindness, not even one; thus by power it has been established twice: once by alteration, once by using the same words, and having omitted the second mentioned 'there is none'. And the 'venom of asps under their lips' is found in those words in use in the 138th psalm; and the 'mouth full of cursing and bitterness' seems to have come from the ninth psalm thus said: his mouth is full of cursing and bitterness and deceit. Next this is: their feet are swift to shed blood; this you will seek in Isaiah or in other editions of the Proverbs, in the hasty to shed blood, which was added with asterisks in the edition of the Seventy. And the 'destruction and misery in their ways' until now I do not know where I have read it, but I think it is written in one of the prophets; and the 'way of peace they have not known' I think in the prophets, and in psalms there is no fear of God before their eyes. Given many sins, not each is guilty of all, but some by this sin, others by that, and thus all by all. We know that whatever the law says to those under the law it speaks, so that every mouth may be closed and all the world may become accountable to God; for by works of law no flesh will be justified before him; for through law comes knowledge of sin. What common to all flesh are the works of the law of Moses? And how does knowledge of sin come through the law of Moses, many and before Moses having known their own sins? Cain indeed says the cause of me is greater to be released; but those who went down to Egypt toward Joseph the patriarchs say concerning the things of Joseph toward.
pass_b_english: First, we must ask: who or what comes initially? Then, who was entrusted next to perceive? It is through the one whom the Spirit grants the word of the serpent and what follows. But if someone mistakenly believes that God’s oracles are merely God’s writings, let them listen to the speaker of the psalm: the Lord’s oracles are pure words, like silver refined in fire, tested on earth, purified sevenfold. I do not think these pure words are the same as the killing letter. Just as the Jews previously mentioned were first entrusted with God’s oracles, so also some disbelieved; yet this unbelief—whether toward God or his oracles—does not annul God’s faithfulness. What then is God’s faithfulness? Is it God believing in some concerning the oracles? Or is it those entrusted with the oracles believing in God, as Abraham believed in God and it was counted to him as righteousness? I think both views have merit; for we must remember both the one who believes in God and the one entrusted with his oracles, especially in the time when scoffers mock believers, so that God’s faithfulness may not be nullified by the words of unbelievers. Let God be true though every human is a liar, as it is written, so that you may be justified in your words and prevail when judged. Therefore, let it be said not as a wish, but as a declaration: may your name be blessed to the ages. What then? Shall we excel? Not at all; for we have charged both Jews and Greeks with being under sin, as it is written: there is none righteous, not even one; none who understands; none who seeks God; all have turned aside, together become worthless; none who does kindness, not even one; their throat is an open grave; with their tongues they practice deceit; the venom of asps lies under their lips; whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness; their feet are swift to shed blood; destruction and misery lie in their ways, and the way of peace they have not known; there is no fear of God before their eyes. He desires to gather explicitly how both Jews and Greeks have come under sin, beginning from what is written: there is none righteous, not even one; none who understands; none who seeks God. We have not found these exact words elsewhere, but we believe they are drawn from the thirteenth and twenty-fifth psalms, altered by the apostle: in the eighteenth psalm, it says the Lord looked down from heaven on the children of men to see if any understand or seek God; and in the twenty-fifth, God looked down from heaven on the children of men to see if any understand or seek God. It seems they equated the act of seeing whether any understand or seek God with the declaration that none understands, none seeks God. I believe the notion of ‘none righteous, not even one’ arises from ‘none does kindness, not even one,’ and thus has been established doubly: once by alteration, once by using identical words while omitting the second mention of ‘there is none.’ The ‘venom of asps under their lips’ appears in the 138th psalm; the ‘mouth full of cursing and bitterness’ seems derived from the ninth psalm: ‘his mouth is full of cursing and bitterness and deceit.’ Next: ‘their feet are swift to shed blood’—this you will find in Isaiah or other editions of Proverbs, in the passage about the hasty to shed blood, which was marked with asterisks in the Septuagint edition. As for ‘destruction and misery in their ways,’ I have not yet located it, but I suspect it is in one of the prophets; likewise, ‘the way of peace they have not known’ I place in the prophets, and in the psalms, ‘there is no fear of God before their eyes.’ Given the multiplicity of sins, not each person is guilty of all, but some by one sin, others by another, and thus all by all. We know that whatever the law says to those under it speaks, so that every mouth may be silenced and all the world held accountable to God; for no flesh will be justified before Him by works of law, since through the law comes knowledge of sin. What is common to all flesh in the works of Moses’ law? And how does knowledge of sin come through Moses’ law, even among many who knew their own sins before Moses? Cain says the cause of me is greater to be released; but those who went down to Egypt toward Joseph the patriarchs speak concerning the things of Joseph, toward…
